land.text: Tripolitania under the British Military Administration

predecessors.note: the Allied administration ran 'from 13 May 1943 until Libyan independence was granted in 1951' (Allied occupation of Libya page); the British administered Tripolitania and Cyrenaica.

land.text: Cyrenaica, proclaimed an emirate by Idris on 1 March 1949

predecessors.note: The Emirate of Cyrenaica page: Idris 'unilaterally proclaimed Cyrenaica an independent Senussi emirate on 1 March 1949'; the Kingdom page lists it as a predecessor. No dossier yet.

land.text: Fezzan-Ghadames: the Fezzan, Ghadames and Ghat, the French military territory

predecessors.note: The Free French occupied the Fezzan from 8 January 1943 and the territory was established on 11 April 1943; it joined Tripolitania and Cyrenaica to form the Kingdom of Libya on 24 December 1951.

land.text: all of Libya, proclaimed after the coup of 1 September 1969

successors.note: 'The monarchy came to an end on 1 September 1969'; Cliopatria's Libyan Arab Republic begins in 1969 with the same outline.

capitals.name: Tripoli
capitals.note: 'Tripoli and Benghazi served alternately as the national capital' (Benghazi: 20.07E, 32.12N); Sabha was the Fezzan's capital.

rulers.name: Idris I
rulers.title: King
rulers.note: Infobox: reign 1951-1969; Hasan is listed for 1962; deposed by the coup of 1 September 1969, which pre-empted an abdication instrument dated 4 August 1969 that would have taken effect on 2 September 1969.

correction.text: the three historic regions united at independence on 24 December 1951

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1951-1952: Cliopatria's row begins in 1953 but the kingdom 'came into existence upon independence on 24 December 1951'. The 1953 outline holds for 1951-1952: Tripolitania, Cyrenaica and Fezzan (area table 276,000 + 850,000 + 631,000 = 1,757,000 km2).

1,613,984 km2 against the provincial areas of 1,757,000 km2 on the page (ratio 0.92; the shape follows the modern Libyan coast and frontiers, about 68 border cells short). Tripolitania, Cyrenaica, Fezzan, Ghadames and Ghat together cover all of it.

1,613,869 km2: one cell different from 1953, a drawing artefact. The southern frontier follows the 1955 treaty between France and Libya, 'based on' the 1899 Anglo-French agreement (Aouzou Strip page); the strip itself (114,000 km2) is Chadian here and was occupied by Libya only in 1973.

1,614,022 km2, the 1953 outline again; the page records no change of boundary, and the kingdom 'enjoyed the advantage of not having aggravated boundary disputes with its neighbors'. The April 1963 unitary reform replaced the three provinces by ten governorates but moved no frontier.
1,614,019 km2, the same outline to the coup.

correction.text: the kingdom's outline until the coup of 1 September 1969

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1969 (January to August): the monarchy lasted until 1 September 1969, but Cliopatria's Kingdom row stops in 1968 and its Libyan Arab Republic row begins in 1969 with the same outline.

region.text: Tripolitania, with Tripoli, the first of the three provinces

ledger.note: 1951: Libya becomes independent on 24 December. 'Independence from the United Kingdom and France: 24 December 1951'; the first country to gain independence through the United Nations (Allied occupation page).

1951: Cyrenaica joins the kingdom on 24 December. 'The independence of the Kingdom of Libya was declared on 24 December 1951'; the Emirate of Cyrenaica, proclaimed by Idris on 1 March 1949, is its predecessor.

region.text: Fezzan-Ghadames: the Fezzan, Ghadames and Ghat, the French military territory

ledger.note: 1951: the Fezzan joins the kingdom on 24 December. The French military territory of Fezzan-Ghadames (administered by France from 1943, military to 1950 and civil 1950-1951) joined Tripolitania and Cyrenaica to form the Kingdom of Libya on 24 December 1951.

1963: the United Kingdom of Libya becomes a unitary Kingdom of Libya in April. 'In April 1963, Prime Minister Mohamed Othman Essed secured adoption by parliament of a bill' replacing the three provinces with ten governorates; no frontier moves.

1969: Gaddafi's officers overthrow King Idris on 1 September. 'The monarchy came to an end on 1 September 1969 when a group of military officers led by' Muammar Gaddafi seized power; the Libyan Arab Republic follows.

certainty.note: The southern desert frontiers with French Africa were still colonial lines; the Egyptian frontier follows the 1925 cession of Jaghbub and Kufra.
The southern frontier rests on 'a 1955 treaty between France and Libya', itself based on the 1899 Anglo-French agreement; Libya disputed it from 1973 (Aouzou Strip).

notes: Cliopatria's Kingdom of Libya has four near-identical shapes (1953-1968; the three changes are one-cell artefacts) and starts in 1953 while the state began on 24 December 1951; its Libyan Arab Republic row starts in 1969 though the kingdom lasted to 1 September 1969, so two new keyframes (1951-1952 and 1969) were added. The shape is the modern Libyan outline: Ghat (attached by France to southern Algeria) and Ghadames (attached to southern Tunisia) are inside it. Counterparts needing dossiers: emirate-of-cyrenaica (1949-1951; Idris proclaimed it 1 March 1949 in Benghazi) and the British Military Administration and French Fezzan-Ghadames territory (1943-1951), for which no Cliopatria row exists (Cliopatria draws Libya as British Africa/French Africa or Italian Africa until 1943, then nothing until 1953); the 1943-1951 gap is a gap-filler task. No wars are listed: the page names none, and records that Libya 'enjoyed the advantage of not having aggravated boundary disputes with its neighbors'. The Anglo-Libyan 20-year treaty of 1953 and the US base agreement of 1954 move no border. Pages silent on: the 1955 treaty's date, Kufra and Jaghbub, Algeria.
